abilities.critical_failure: As failure, 100 feet back and knocked prone, taking 50 bludgeoning damage from the fall.
abilities.critical_success: The creature takes 1d12 force damage and is pushed 5 feet away from the manor.
abilities.effect: An explosive blast of magic violently slams against the intruder, who must attempt a DC 33 Reflex save. If the triggering creature isn't adjacent to the manor, it adjusts the result of this save up by one degree of success.
abilities.failure: The creature takes 4d12+16 force damage and is thrown 20 feet back and knocked prone, taking 10 bludgeoning damage from the fall.
abilities.name: Denied
abilities.success: The creature takes 2d12+13 force damage and is pushed 5 feet away from the manor.
abilities.trigger: A creature without a nullifying seal script on their hand approaches within 5 feet of the manor or attempts to damage the manor

hazard.description: Layers of fulus and strips of prayer-printed ribbons are plastered over the walls and entrances to the manor, demarcating a boundary around the mansion where no ghosts or spirits can pass.
hazard.disable: DC 35 Arcana, Occultism, or Thievery (master) to compromise the magic to allow entry into the manor, DC 32 Athletics to force your way through the barrier and enter the manor (this doesn't allow other PCs to enter behind you, though!), or *dispel magic* (5th level; counteract DC 28) to counteract the wards
hazard.name: Manor Wards
hazard.reset: The wards reset automatically, continuing to prevent entry and damaging those attempting to bypass until they’re disabled.

traits.name: Unique
traits.text: A rules element with this trait is one-of-a-kind. The DC of Recall Knowledge checks related to creatures with this trait is increased by 10.

traits.name: Environmental
traits.text: A hazard with this trait is something dangerous that’s part of the natural world, such as quicksand or harmful mold.

traits.name: Magical
traits.text: Something with the magical trait is imbued with magical energies not tied to a specific tradition of magic. Some items or effects are closely tied to a particular tradition of magic. In these cases, the item has the arcane, divine, occult, or primal trait instead of the magical trait. Any of these traits indicate that the item is magical.
